answering.finding_2: the shared execution identity, which was the whole remainder

the_identity_reaches_both_vectors.how_without_a_signature_growing_a_uid: `workspaces.identity_for(group)` derives the identity behind the deployment's already-minted `WorkspaceGroup`: the gid is the group's, and the uid is `os.geteuid()` -- who this manager actually is. Both vectors already receive that capability, so NOTHING anywhere grew a uid operand a caller could choose. That is the property the pinned `65532:65532` was protecting, and it is kept.
the_identity_reaches_both_vectors.execution: `oci.run_vector` substitutes `--user <uid>:<gid>` at the RESTRICTIONS table, exactly where `--network` is already substituted, so there is still one `--user` in the argv and a reader still sees the whole posture in the table.
the_identity_reaches_both_vectors.custody: `custody.custody_vector` substitutes the same pair. The custodian exists to OWN what the worker created -- that is the whole mechanism, and under a shared identity 'the same uid the worker ran as' is this manager's own.
the_identity_reaches_both_vectors.consent_is_untouched: a consent runtime mounts nothing and writes nothing this manager reads back, so it keeps the pinned pair and is still refused a supplementary group. A probe proved the posture condition is what keeps consent COMPOSING at all, not merely what keeps its uid pinned.

requested_is_not_observed.why_it_matters_here: `test_worker_entry_engine` measured THIS host relabelling a container-created file to uid 65534, the kernel's overflow id. A daemon with an id mapping silently relabels everything the worker writes, and an identity shared on only one side of the boundary is not shared.
requested_is_not_observed.what_was_added: `workspaces.supported_identity_mapping(identity, observed_identity)` asks of an OBSERVATION -- the host-side (uid, gid) of something the runtime actually created. An unmeasured mapping is refused with its own sentence, a remapped one is refused naming both pairs and what an operator can do about it, and a matching one answers the identity.
requested_is_not_observed.NOT_YET_WIRED_TO_A_LIVE_OBSERVATION: the decision function exists and is checked; the seam that feeds it a real host-side observation at start, before affected effects, is NOT written. Stated plainly rather than implied: today nothing calls it in the launch path, so a remapping engine is not yet refused in production.

delivered_this_claim.the_supplementary_group_revalidated_rath: under the shared identity the PRIMARY gid is already the workspace group, so `--group-add` is redundant -- and it is kept because it is the grant that survives if a deployment ever runs the manager under another primary group, which is the case W33936/M34916 was written for. A check asserts both the substituted `--user` and the retained `--group-add`.
